title.en: Words that go together in sport

es: Reconocer combinaciones naturales de verbo y sustantivo en textos deportivos: score a goal, break a record, take part in.

teaching.en: Leo wants to score a goal in every match.
teaching.es: Leo quiere marcar un gol en cada partido.
teaching.explanationEs: Los goles se marcan: score a goal. En inglés no se dice «make a goal».
teaching.audioText: Leo wants to score a goal in every match.

teaching.en: Our team can break the record if we win this race.
teaching.es: Nuestro equipo puede batir el récord si ganamos esta carrera.
teaching.explanationEs: Break a record = batir un récord. Win se usa con carreras, partidos y premios.
segments: Our team can break the record
teaching.audioText: Our team can break the record if we win this race.

teaching.en: Ana won a gold medal, and Tom won a silver medal.
teaching.es: Ana ganó una medalla de oro y Tom ganó una de plata.
teaching.explanationEs: Win a medal: el verbo de los premios es win, no «gain».
segments: Ana won a gold medal, and
teaching.audioText: Ana won a gold medal, and Tom won a silver medal.

teaching.en: My brother plays for a small team, but they beat the best team in the city.
teaching.es: Mi hermano juega en un equipo pequeño, pero derrotaron al mejor equipo de la ciudad.
teaching.explanationEs: A un rival se le derrota: beat a team. Win va con el partido, no con el rival.
segments: My brother plays for a small team, but
they beat the best team in the city.
teaching.audioText: My brother plays for a small team, but they beat the best team in the city.

teaching.en: Many people take part in the city race every spring.
teaching.es: Mucha gente participa en la carrera de la ciudad cada primavera.
teaching.explanationEs: Take part in = participar en; la preposición in va siempre al final.
teaching.audioText: Many people take part in the city race every spring.
